biothings.name: cleft lip/palate-intestinal malrotation-cardiopathy syndrome
biothings.definition: Cleft lip/palate - intestinal malrotation - cardiopathy is a multiple congenital anomaly syndrome described in 5 patients to date, characterized by flat face, hypertelorism, flat occiput, upward slanting palpebral fissures, cleft palate, micrognathia, short neck, and severe congenital heart defects which were lethal in 3 of the 5 patients reported. Malrotation of the intestine, bilateral clinodactyly, bilobed tongue, short fourth metatarsals and bifid thumbs were reported in individual cases. There have been no further descriptions in the literature since 1997. [Orphanet:2001]

biothings.name: volvulus of midgut
biothings.definition: A congenital abnormality in which the intestine is abnormally rotated (twisted). It may result in intestinal obstruction. [NCIT:C98961]
biothings.synonyms: congenital malrotation of intestine, intestinal malrotation, volvulus of midgut

biothings.name: intestinal volvulus
biothings.definition: Twisting of a loop of bowel that results in intestinal obstruction. [NCIT:P378]

opentargets.name: growth delay-hydrocephaly-lung hypoplasia syndrome
opentargets.description: Growth delay - hydrocephaly - lung hypoplasia, also named Game-Friedman-Paradice syndrome, is a rare developmental disorder described in 4 sibs so far and characterized by delayed fetal growth, hydrocephaly with patent aqueduct of Sylvius, underdeveloped lungs and various other anomalies such as small jaw, intestinal malrotation, omphalocele, shortness of lower limbs, bowed tibias and foot deformities.

opentargets.name: hypoplastic pancreas-intestinal atresia-hypoplastic gallbalder syndrome
opentargets.description: Hypoplastic pancreas-intestinal atresia-hypoplastic gallbladder syndrome is a rare, potentially fatal, genetic, visceral malformation syndrome characterized by neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, duodenal and jejunal atresia, as well as gallbladder aplasia or hypoplasia. Patients typically present intrauterine growth restriction, failure to thrive, malnutrition, intestinal malrotation, malabsorption, conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, acholia and infections. Cardiac anomalies may also be associated.
